methodologyMarkdown:
## Overview
UN Women's Digital Library is a Drupal-based catalog of ~968 publications, fully server-rendered. The listing page embeds publication cards, extensive facets (26 resource types, 90+ topics, regions, countries, publishers, series) and pagination directly in the HTML, so it is reliably scrapable without a JavaScript engine.

## Search
Full-text search is handled by a separate site-wide endpoint: /en/search-results?querytext={query}. Results are server-rendered but mix publications with other content types, so post-filtering by URL path (/digital-library/publications/) is recommended.

## Filters
Facets appear in the HTML as query-parameter links (resource type, topic, region, country, publisher, series). These can be composed onto the listing URL for filtered browsing, but no formal filter schema/API is published, so they are treated as opaque URL params rather than declared filters.

## Download
Cards link to record pages using /en/digital-library/publications/{year}/{month}/{slug}. Each record page exposes the actual PDF (typically under /sites/default/files/). A two-step crawl (listing -> record -> PDF) is required; PDFs are not linked directly from the listing.

## Metadata & Enrichment
Title, publication date, resource type and topic tags are present in both the listing and record pages. There is no JSON/REST API, so enrichment is limited to HTML parsing.

## Limitations
No public API. Pagination uses ?page=N (0-indexed). The site sits behind a CDN; automated clients should send a realistic User-Agent to avoid WAF challenges. Search results require type-filtering.
